slides.title: Former NFL QB Matt Hasselbeck volunteers his brain for CTE research in hopes of finding a diagnosis in the living
slides.body:
<<<INDENT>>>Chronic traumatic encephalopathy — CTE — is a debilitating, degenerative brain disease linked to repeated head trauma from playing football. For now, there's no way to diagnose CTE while someone is alive.
<<<INDENT>>>Matt Hasselbeck is working with Boston University to find a method to detect CTE in living people. The Associated Press reported on these efforts Wednesday.

<<<INDENT>>>(cont) Hasselbeck recently spent two days with Boston University, volunteering his body and brain to undergo a series of tests to determine the extent to which his playing career and the repeated head trauma that came with it has affected his brain health. 
<<<INDENT>>>Hasselbeck told AP that the tests included a blood sample, an MRI on his brain and a PET (positron emission tomography) scan that injects a radioactive tracer that maps out the brain's function.
